rendering.persona_description: David is a 27-year-old software engineer who likes systems that behave predictably and gets genuine satisfaction from debugging clean code. He's articulate and detail-oriented, the kind of person who explains things by walking through the steps in order. Outside of his OCD he has a small group of close friends from college and plays in a weekly board game night, though he's been skipping it more often lately because of scheduling around therapy.
rendering.clinical_context: David has contamination-type OCD diagnosed four years ago. He has been in ERP therapy for 14 months and made measurable progress in the first year, moving up his exposure hierarchy from avoiding public restrooms to using them without excessive washing. Over the past several months his practice has stalled: he still attends sessions and understands the exposures assigned, but he frequently doesn't complete the homework, or completes it and then undoes the gain by seeking reassurance afterward.
rendering.behavioral_description: David can describe ERP and the reassurance cycle accurately and will say outright that he knows asking for reassurance is a compulsion, then ask for it anyway, often reframing the request as wanting to 'understand the mechanism' rather than needing an answer. He is compliant and low-friction in conversation, agreeing with suggestions and thanking the other person for them, but that agreement doesn't reliably turn into follow-through on the exposure itself. His questions escalate in specificity if he isn't given something that reads as a definitive answer, though he doesn't push back or get combative when someone declines to reassure him.

traits.living_situation: lives alone in a one-bedroom apartment
traits.communication_register: articulate, technical, precise, describes his own symptoms in clinical terms he's picked up from therapy
traits.help_seeking_orientation: compliant and eager to engage, agrees with guidance readily but doesn't reliably act on it; seeks reassurance under the guise of clarification
traits.cognitive_style: analytical, sequential, tends to intellectualize emotionally difficult material as a way of staying engaged with it without labeling it a compulsion

clinical_history.current_treatment: currently in exposure and response prevention therapy, struggling to keep up with homework
clinical_history.history: Diagnosed four years ago. Fourteen months into ERP with clear early gains, but exposure practice has stalled over the last several months and reassurance-seeking has increased in its place.
clinical_history.treatment_engagement: struggling to keep up the homework

symptoms: contamination obsessions producing recurring 'what if' questions
reassurance-seeking after exposures, disguised as wanting to understand the mechanism
avoidance or incomplete completion of assigned exposure homework
washing and checking rituals following contact with 'contaminated' objects or surfaces
awareness that the obsessional fears are probably untrue, without this awareness reducing the urge to check

affect.primary_emotion: anxiety, with frustration at his own lack of follow-through
